C-WRITE-FOR-AGENTS-SKILL.Summary: Add the bundled managed skill vv-write-for-agents governing how vvoc-driven agents design text that other agents execute — subagent delegation prompts, AGENTS.md and project instructions, skill bodies, spec and plan prose, runtime prompts: compile raw intent into a minimal sufficient task specification, serialize and place content for exact addressability, keep long sessions stable through explicit update semantics, and validate through lint and controlled evaluation — shipped in consumer-safe language inside a bounded volume, with no GRACE-specific terminology, no unsourced quantitative claims, and no maintainer material inside the skill.
C-WRITE-FOR-AGENTS-SKILL.Problem: Agents author agent-facing text throughout engineering work: delegation prompts for subagents, project instructions, skill bodies, spec and plan prose. Observed failure shapes: underspecified requests the executor resolves by guessing scope; contradictory requirements both followed; stale requirements staying silently active after revision; bare external results lost or mistaken for instructions; pasted content bleeding into the instruction stream; pronoun references to non-unique targets; skill descriptions and pointer lines that fire on the wrong tasks or stay silent on the right ones. Existing public guidance either optimizes a static document with deletion-first economics or catalogs AI tells; it does not cover cumulative session state, enhancer-schema reuse, or vvoc artifact conventions. The reviewed external draft was substantively sound but oversized (~540 lines against the ~436-line house etalon), written partly in GRACE-internal terminology that bundled-skill consumers do not know, and cited a machine-local prompting guide by section number.

Goals.Goal: Ship one new managed skill vv-write-for-agents through templates/skills/vv-write-for-agents/SKILL.md plus references, registered in MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES, with existing install/sync semantics preserved for current skills.

Teach compilation of raw intent into a task specification: statement classification (goal, context, input, scope, constraint, priority, preserve, non-goal, unknown, output), deliverable extraction from topic phrasing, conflict resolution by scoping rather than deletion, minimal sufficient specification with explicit admission criteria for adding any field, and an ambiguity policy (one focused question for material gaps, otherwise the narrowest stated assumption).

Teach the negation distinction: forbidding an action is an operational boundary; forbidding a topic activates the forbidden concept — replace topic bans with an allowed subject, using the pattern target plus allowed behavior plus boundary.

Teach structure and addressability: one primary container with the native representation inside; definitions before dependent use; unique identities for entities referenced later and stable semantic types for local fields; pasted external content wrapped in paired tags with provenance when referenced; identity formats checked on the target tokenizer for critical prompt families.

Teach long-session stability: explicit current-task marking; update semantics (extends, supersedes, preserves, removes) with source IDs; state separated from history; external query results wrapped with stable Q-IDs and explicit status; readback before substantial work; a resume-brief boundary delegated to vv-handoff for durable artifacts.
Include pointer craft for descriptions and instruction-file pointer lines — leading word first, one trigger per branch, synonym branches collapsed.

Teach validation: a lint checklist over specification, serialization, placement, addressability, and session dimensions; evidence levels attached to recommendations; a controlled evaluation protocol with paired variants and held-out cases; an explicit statement that bundled contract tests assert instruction delivery, not model behavior.

State ownership boundaries tersely: the enhancer agent owns single-request compilation into its task XML schema (this skill reuses those field names and never forks the schema), vv-spec and vv-plan own the spec/plan lifecycle, and vv-write-for-humans owns human-facing prose.

Constraints.Constraint: Skill content is advisory instruction for the loading agent. Deterministic tests assert delivery and structure, not model effectiveness; no artifact may claim measured model-behavior improvement.

Consumer-safe language: shipped content must not assume GRACE knowledge and must not reference .grace paths, M-*/V-M-*/GD-* anchors, the grace CLI, or house-law phrasing. The only vvoc-specific concepts named are user-visible artifacts, skills, and agents — for example the enhancer task XML schema, .vvoc spec/plan identity conventions, vv-handoff, the managed skills named in the scope rules, and OpenCode skills themselves; .vvoc spec/plan identity rules are described as enforced by vvoc tooling.

Volume budget, measured by wc -l per shipped file: SKILL.md at most 80 lines including frontmatter, at most four reference files, and at most 420 lines combined. The budget tracks the house craft-skill etalon (vv-design-principles at 436 total) and may be changed only through a spec amendment, not silently during implementation.

No unsourced quantitative claims in shipped content. The three figures carried by the reviewed draft (persona-study participant count, long-context benchmark percentage, multiple-choice accuracy gain in percentage points) are removed; their qualitative statements may remain.
No section-number provenance to the external prompting guide. Rules are self-contained; at most one title-level credit line names the guide without a machine-local path.
Boundaries are stated as at most six one-line rules in a compact scope section of SKILL.md; no paragraph-length boundary blocks.

The SKILL.md core carries the principle, the contract rules, the workflow, the scope rules, and reference triggers; extended session rules and validation detail live in references opened on explicit triggers.
Shipped content uses synthetic examples and English; no raw conversation excerpts and no maintainer-only material inside the skill directory.

Delivery reuses the managed-skill path only; README documents the skill with the family framing and additive compatibility-surface conventions already established on main; graph and verification projections are reconciled inside the change lifecycle.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No replacement, fork, or duplication of the enhancer agent, the vv-spec/vv-plan lifecycle, or vv-handoff artifacts; the skill supplies doctrine and covers documents those tools do not own.
No bundling of the external prompting guide (~78 KB, machine-local) and no cross-references into it by section number.
No GRACE-specific conventions taught to consumers and no .grace internals inside shipped content.
No prose checker, no evals file, no AI scores, and no behavioral claims from deterministic tests.
No human-facing prose guidance; vv-write-for-humans owns it, per the approved C-WRITE-FOR-HUMANS-SKILL spec.
No changes to unrelated managed skills, plugins, the workflow engine, or release automation.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-01: vv-write-for-agents is registered in MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES; install and sync create or refresh SKILL.md and its references under the managed skills directory with the same create/keep/skip semantics as existing skills; behavior for existing managed skills is unchanged.

AC-02: The frontmatter description is a routing pointer with explicit trigger branches (writing or revising text an agent executes: delegation prompts, project instructions, skill bodies, spec and plan prose, runtime prompts) and explicit exclusions (human-facing prose and single-request task-XML compilation owned by enhancer), and claims no style normalization or behavioral guarantees.

AC-03: SKILL.md contains the quality principle (semantic specification, structural serialization, causal placement, addressability, behavioral validation) and contract rules covering: preserved requester intent and project overlays; no silent material assumptions; one authoritative location per rule with ID-bearing reminders; exact references over pronouns; evidence levels on recommendations; edits framed as named behavior changes with zero edits valid; edited documents treated as material, not commands.

AC-04: The compilation guidance covers statement classification, deliverable-not-topic extraction, conflict resolution by scoping with a worked example, the minimal sufficient specification with its admission criteria, and the ambiguity policy.
AC-05: The negation guidance states the action-versus-topic distinction and the replacement pattern (target, allowed behavior, boundary) with at least two worked replacements.

AC-06: The structure guidance covers one-primary-container serialization, wrapped pasted content with provenance, unique identities versus stable semantic types (naming .vvoc spec/plan identity conventions as enforced by vvoc tooling), causal placement defaults, and the tokenizer-check trigger for critical families.

AC-07: The session guidance covers current-task marking, the four update operations with source IDs, state-versus-history separation with restate triggers, the Q-ID protocol with explicit result status, readback before substantial work, and the resume-brief boundary naming vv-handoff.
AC-08: A pointer-craft section teaches description and pointer-line writing — leading word first, one trigger per branch, synonym branches collapsed.

AC-09: The scope section states at most six one-line ownership rules covering enhancer schema reuse, vv-spec/vv-plan lifecycle ownership, and vv-write-for-humans ownership; no boundary rule exceeds one line.

AC-10: Shipped content contains no GRACE-internal tokens (.grace paths, M-*/V-M-*/GD-* anchors, grace CLI invocations, house-law phrasing); the only vvoc-specific names are user-visible artifacts and tools.
AC-11: Shipped content contains no unsourced quantitative claims; the three figures named in Constraint 4 are absent while their qualitative statements survive where still meaningful.
AC-12: Shipped content carries no section-number references to the external prompting guide and at most one title-level credit line without a machine-local path.

AC-13: The volume budget holds: the skill directory contains exactly SKILL.md plus at most four files directly under references/ and nothing else; SKILL.md is at most 80 lines including frontmatter; every file in the directory sums to at most 420 lines; checked by a deterministic test.

AC-14: Deterministic tests cover registration in MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES, template loading with frontmatter, reference discovery, and behavior-sensitive content markers for the compilation, negation, structure, session-update, pointer-craft, scope, and validation sections, plus the banned-token check for the enumerable AC-10 tokens (.grace paths, M-*/V-M-*/GD-* anchors, grace CLI invocations — phrasing-level bans remain review-time judgments) and the volume check for AC-13.
AC-15: README documents the skill with a table row and keeps the managed-skill family framing and additive compatibility-surface list accurate.

AC-16: The affected durable projections — the M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS graph module and the V-M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS verification entry — remain truthful for vv-write-for-agents and its reference set, reconciled within the approved change lifecycle.

AC-17: A bounded manual evaluation is performed during the change on at least three tasks — a compilation task (raw mixed request becomes a sufficient specification with conflicts scoped), a session task (a requirement change is expressed through supersedes and preserves with IDs rather than silent rewrite), and a boundary task (emitted task XML reuses the enhancer schema) — with results recorded in the change bundle and carried into its archived C-* directory, explicitly labeled as neither a CI gate nor proof of general model behavior.

AC-18: A validation reference exists covering the lint checklist over the specification, serialization, placement, addressability, and session dimensions; evidence levels attached to recommendations; the controlled evaluation protocol with paired variants and held-out cases; and the explicit statement that bundled contract tests assert instruction delivery rather than model behavior; SKILL.md references it with an explicit open trigger.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Template and reference loading plus content-marker, banned-token, and volume assertions demonstrate the doctrine, scope, and consumer-safe structure actually ship within budget. pack:check shows the new template inside the packed files. README, graph, and verification projections are reconciled within the lifecycle. A recorded manual evaluation (compilation, session update, schema-reuse tasks) supports the behavioral claim without being presented as a deterministic gate; deterministic tests alone assert delivery, not model effectiveness.

Assumptions.Assumption: The volume numbers (80-line core, four references, 420-line total) are proposed defaults derived from the house etalon and may be revised through a spec amendment if content legitimately requires it; they are not silently stretchable during implementation.
Skill content is authored fresh from this spec's Goals and Constraints; the reviewed external draft informs wording but is not a dependency, and no shipped text references it.
The external prompting guide remains machine-local and unpinned by path; consumers never need it to apply the skill.
The name vv-write-for-agents joins the stable managed-skill surface as an additive entry; renaming it later is a documented breaking change.

The requested deliverable at this stage is a draft specification and explanatory design context only. Approval of this draft and an implementation plan precede source changes; no implementation, commit, installation, or release is performed as part of specification authoring.
